candidates.source_body_excerpt: A mountain rescue team helped police find a missing dementia sufferer from Rochdale. The 71-year-old was reported missing on Saturday, with Greater Manchester Police and a police helicopter joining the search near the Piethorne Reservoir area of Newhey. Police called in Oldham Mountain Rescue Team to help with the search and volunteers located the man on Saturday night. The team shared: “The team was called to assist GMP who requested assistance with the search for a 71-year-old male with dementia who was missing in the Piethorne Reservoir area of Newhey. “The individual had an air tag that was indicating he was in the area of the reservoir. Initial searches by the police, including a search by the NPAS helicopter, had not provided any further information. “The team mobilised, along with the water section, to the dam wall at Piethorne Reservoir. “Our water team commenced a search of the water’s edge either side of the dam wall, both on foot and on the water using the raft. Two further section began searches of the paths and tracks not already covered by the police. “Search dogs were requested with two dogs responding. The first dog, with its handler and a navigator from the team, was on the way to their allocated search area when they found the individual, who was cold and confused.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Courteeners frontman Liam Fray revisits The Briton's Protection Pub in Manchester where he first performed more than 20 years ago The street outside legendary indie club 42s, a front garden on Burnage Lane and a pub's function room with a tiny stage - all locations in Manchester where you could have found Courteeners in their early days. The four school friends from Middleton, near Rochdale, have certainly come a long way since they hit the Manchester indie scene in 2006. While they have travelled around the world ever since, there is no place like home and they will take to the stage later for a huge homecoming gig at Wythenshawe Park. From humble beginnings performing for friends in the garden of their shared house in Burnage, the Courteeners are now celebrating 20 years together. Fresh from releasing a new best-of compilation album called God Bless The Band, lead singer and songwriter Liam Fray spoke to BBC North West Tonight at The Briton's Protection pub on Deansgate, where he first performed as a solo artist back in 2005. candidates.source_title: MATCH PREVIEW: U's CHASE BACK-TO-BACK WINS AGAINST ROCHDALE AFC - Colchester United FC
candidates.source_summary: U's Chase Back-To-Back wins against Rochdale AFC - What you need to know as old faces return to the JCS...
candidates.source_body_excerpt: <h3>What you need to know as old faces return to the JCS...</h3> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h4>The Match</h4> <p>The U&rsquo;s take on Rochdale AFC at the JobServe Community Stadium on Saturday 29th August.</p> <p>Danny and Nicky&rsquo;s side head into the game on the back of their first League Two win of the season, beating Oldham Athletic 2-1 at the JobServe Community Stadium last time out. Harry Anderson&rsquo;s second-half leveller and a stoppage-time Lewis Temple own goal secured all three points. Academy striker Kien Connolly is expected to keep his place in the matchday squad following his senior debut against Oldham.</p> <p>This weekend&rsquo;s match offers the U&rsquo;s the chance to build on that result and pick up back-to-back league wins, ahead of a week of away fixtures &ndash; a trip to <a href="https://tickets.colchesterunited.net/Tickets/BuyTickets/SeatSelection/40202" target="_blank">Bristol Rovers in midweek on Tuesday 1st September</a> and a journey to <a href="https://tickets.colchesterunited.net/Tickets/BuyTickets/SeatSelection/40206" target="_blank">Swindon Town on Saturday 5<sup>th</sup> September.</a> Tickets for these away fixtures are still available to purchase until Sunday and Thursday, respectively.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h4>The Opponents</h4> <p>Rochdale AFC, known as the Dale, arrive at the JobServe Community Stadium having lost both of their opening two League Two fixtures, going down 3-0 away at Newport County before falling to a 1-2 home defeat to Crawley Town last Saturday.</p> <p>The Dale return to the Football League for the first time since their relegation to the National League at the end of the 2022/23 season, having won promotion via the play-offs with a penalty shoot-out victory over Boreham Wood at Wembley in May after finishing runners-up behind champions York City.</p> <p>Rochdale&rsquo;s route into this season&rsquo;s League Two campaign also included a Carabao Cup exit, beating Tranmere Rovers on penalties in the preliminary round before going down 2-0 away to League One side Bradford City in round one.</p> <p>Head coach Ian Watson took charge of the Dale in June, joining from National League North side South Shields, where he led the club to a second-place finish and a promotion final appearance in his first full season in charge. He replaced Jimmy McNulty, who departed for League One club Stockport County.</p> <p>Watson has overseen a significant rebuild over the summer, with new arrivals including goalkeeper Nils Ramming, centre-back Laurence Maguire, and Chelsea loanee Kaiden Wilson, alongside forwards Cian Hayes and Zain Silcott-Duberry. Saturday could also mark a return to Essex for the ever-present Ian Henderson. In a period spanning three years, the striker netted 26 goals and provided nine assists in 129 appearances for the U&rsquo;s in the early 2010s.</p> <p>The two sides have not met since the 2022/23 season, when a first-half Devante Rodney penalty gave Rochdale a 1-0 win at the JobServe Community Stadium in September 2022 before the U&rsquo;s claimed all three points in Greater Manchester in January 2023.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h4>The Matchday</h4> <p>We&rsquo;re at home in Sky Bet League Two action once again!

candidates.source_body_excerpt: By SOPHIE CHURCH - POLITICAL REPORTER 16:03 28 Aug 2026, updated 16:19 28 Aug 2026 Ed Miliband ’s efforts to deport the ringleader of the Rochdale grooming gang came to nothing this week after Pakistan refused to take him back. Mohammad Ishaq Dar, Pakistan’s deputy prime minister and foreign minister, informed Mr Miliband in a meeting on Thursday Pakistan would not accept Shabir Ahmed back because it was not legally bound to do so. Pakistani officials told their British counterparts they ‘currently do not have any legislation or formal mechanism under which we can take him back’. Ahmed, who was convicted of 30 child rape offences, was released in July this year after serving 14 years behind bars. While he has been stripped of his British citizenship, ministers are facing difficulties deporting him because Commonwealth citizens arriving in Britain before 1973 are protected from removal under archaic legislation. Pakistan has long claimed Ahmed is Britain’s responsibility as he renounced his Pakistani citizenship long ago, and has spent virtually his entire life in the UK . Mr Miliband, who Andy Burnham made Foreign Secretary on entering No 10, pressed Mr Dar to consider taking the criminal back in a meeting at the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office for the pair's first meeting.

candidates.source_title: Step back in time with historic town centre landmark - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_summary: The restoration of a unique set of historic steps which are more than 400 years old old has been completed in the heart of Rochdale town centre.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The restoration of a unique set of historic steps which are more than 400 years old old has been completed in the heart of Rochdale town centre. Running through the Broadfield Park Slopes, the Packer Spout steps link the major historic attractions of Rochdale Town Hall and its surrounding area to St Chad’s Church, the oldest church in the borough, parts of which have Saxon origins. Dating from sometime before 1660, the church steps have a rich history and were thought to be used by mourning relatives who would travel up the steps to St Chad’s Church, where they would scatter rue and rosemary in ‘God’s Acre’ (St Chad’s Churchyard) as an offering to ease the spirits of their loved ones. Situated in the recently restored Broadfield Park Slopes area, during the Victorian period, the steps ran directly through a notorious slum area, known as ‘the gank’. The gank was characterised by tightly packed housing, narrow passageways, high crime rates and large numbers of ‘houses of ill repute’. Many of the residents who worked in Rochdale’s mills would have lived out their lives in this area. The site is so steep that Oldham contractor Maysand, which delivered the work, had to devise a special pulley system with tracks and rollers to help transport the stone up the hill. READ MORE: Police target organised gang over 19 violent Parklife robberies The team had to painstakingly remove all 122 steps, many of which had become broken and uneven, before reconstructing both the area underneath and the damaged steps using traditional sandstone, to match the existing stone.
